enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

1101 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1020 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026

 - Breezy winds expected ahead of a Pacific cold front this
   afternoon. West winds will gust up to 45 mph along east facing
   slopes and exposed ridgelines.

 - Cooler temperatures and fair weather are expected for most of
   next week. Freeze Warning in effect for several southern New
   Mexico locales early tomorrow morning.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1020 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026

Breezy winds will accompany a Pacific cold front moving in tandem
with an upper-level trough across the Rockies this afternoon.
Winds could occasionally gust up to 40 mph (50 mph in the 
Sacramento Mountains). Dust is not expected with these winds. 
Skies will range from mostly sunny to partly cloudy today as 
temperatures fall to 2-8 degrees below normal.

High pressure will build in tonight, and how much radiational 
cooling the desert lowlands of New Mexico (north of Cruces) could
see will hinge on how fast the winds diminish. Dewpoints dropping
into the upper-10s to lower-20s and a lack of cloud cover will 
help. The weakest gradient will be north of the I-10 corridor in 
New Mexico. Upper-10s in the Gila cold spots are likely. The 
Jornada Range and the Hatch Valley look like a fair bet for 
reaching the freezing mark, hence the Freeze Warning. The Mesilla 
Valley is a 50/50 toss-up. We'll get another chance Sunday 
night/Monday morning as winds will be lighter. 

Benign weather is favored early next week, though another passing
trough early Tuesday morning could produce a mix of wintry
precipitation in the northern Sacramento Mountains. Calm weather
for Wednesday, though the models are in disagreement on Thursday
with the pattern across the CONUS.

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1020 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026

Gusty west winds up to 20G30KT expected for the afternoon as a 
cold front passes through. Winds will shift to the northwest and
diminish in the early evening. VFR conditions expected for the
entire period, and ceilings will be unlimited, though some periods
of BKN070-100 in the afternoon are likely.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1020 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026

Breezy west winds for the afternoon by way of a passing Pacific
cold front, with gusts up to 50 mph in the Sacramento Mountains.
These gusts will persist for a few hours before shifting
northwest and diminishing in the early evening. Min RHs will be at
or above 20% for the rest of the coming week, and winds will
generally be calmer early next week. Ventilation rates will be
Very Good to Excellent this afternoon and Fair to Good tomorrow.

&&
